1	"""Read-only audit replication batches.
2	
3	A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
4	whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::
5	
6	    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}
7	
8	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
9	``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
10	1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
11	up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
12	than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
13	order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
14	``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
15	when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
16	batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
17	true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
18	audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
19	CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
20	
21	:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
22	appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
23	key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
24	the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
25	written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
26	``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
27	present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
28	:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
29	only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
30	last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
31	and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
32	``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.
33	
34	Batches are checked only against the byte contract: canonical encoding, key
35	order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
36	enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the kind enum, non-empty
37	string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every log :func:`audit.read`
38	accepts round-trips through :func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The
39	append itself is atomic: when the write, flush or fsync step raises
40	:class:`OSError` the error propagates unchanged and the log is left
41	byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was missing).
42	
43	:func:`apply_remote` persists remote state applications in a version-1
44	*ledger*: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys sorted lexicographically,
45	exactly one trailing ``\\n``) with the top-level keys ``audit``,
46	``requests``, ``state`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
47	``state`` holds the current :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state,
48	``requests`` binds each accepted request id to the digest of its request,
49	and ``audit`` lists one entry per successful application in order; each
50	entry carries ``after``/``before`` state digests, the request ``id`` and
51	``source`` and a contiguous ``seq`` starting at 1, every entry after the
52	first chaining its ``before`` to the previous entry's ``after`` and the
53	last ``after`` hashing the stored state.  A missing ledger stands for the
54	request's ``base`` state with empty indexes; any existing file that fails
55	the byte, structure, state or index rules is rejected with
56	:class:`ValueError` and left untouched.
57	
58	Replaying a request whose ``id`` is already bound to exactly the same
59	request digest always yields ``duplicate`` from the saved binding alone,
60	immediately or after other commits: one item per remote record in
61	ascending key order, each already duplicate with an empty ``need`` map,
62	and no receipt; the ledger is never read for modification on a replay.
63	A bound ``id`` presented with a different request raises
64	:class:`ValueError`.  Every successful commit is one durable transaction:
65	write, flush, file sync, replacement and directory sync all lie inside
66	its boundary, and an :class:`OSError` at any stage propagates unchanged
67	with the file system restored to its pre-call state.
68	
69	Each commit is additionally backed by a *recovery intent* so a crash of
70	the committing process itself can be reconciled later, across processes.
71	Before anything is replaced, the commit publishes an intent at ``path +
72	".txn"``: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys recursively sorted,
73	exactly one trailing ``\n``) recording only ``version`` (the integer 1),
74	``phase``, the lowercase hex SHA-256 digests of the new and old ledger
75	bytes (``newDigest``/``oldDigest``) and the safe base names of the
76	candidate and predecessor transaction files, all confined to the
77	ledger's own directory; when the ledger did not exist, ``oldDigest`` and
78	``predecessor`` are both ``null``.  The intent starts in phase
79	``prepared`` and is republished as ``installed`` only after the new
80	ledger has replaced the old one and the directory has synced; the
81	intent's own creation and phase change each sync the file and the
82	directory.  A crash before the ``installed`` intent is durable leaves
83	the commit unconfirmed: :func:`recover_ledger` keeps or restores the old
84	bytes (byte-for-byte, and missing again when the path was missing) and
85	deletes the referenced candidate.  A crash afterwards lets
86	:func:`recover_ledger` verify the new bytes against ``newDigest`` and
87	finish the cleanup.  Only files the intent references are removed, the
88	intent itself is deleted last and the directory is synced, and a
89	repeated call reports ``clean`` without scanning random artifacts.
90	
91	:func:`recover_ledger` returns a fresh dict with the key order
92	``digest``, ``status``: ``clean`` when no intent exists, ``rolled-back``
93	or ``completed`` after a recovery, with ``digest`` holding the digest of
94	the resulting ledger bytes (``None`` when the path is missing).  A
95	``path`` that is not a str raises :class:`TypeError`; an intent that
96	fails to parse, or whose fields, phase, names, digests or necessary
97	artifacts are invalid, raises :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` (a
98	:class:`ValueError`) without touching the ledger or any unrelated file;
99	an :class:`OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing
100	propagates unchanged with enough intent and artifacts left for a retry.
101	The ledger write entry points run this recovery automatically after
102	their input validation, before the ledger is read.
103	
104	:func:`inspect_recovery` diagnoses an explicit, non-empty list of ledger
105	paths without modifying anything: only each listed ledger, its intent
106	and the artifacts the intent references are read.  Each report carries
107	``path``, ``status``, ``phase``, ``digest``, ``artifacts``, ``action``
108	and ``error`` -- ``clean`` with a null phase and action when no intent
109	exists (the digest still summarizes the ledger bytes, or is null when
110	the path is missing), ``pending`` with the intent's phase and the
111	suggested action (``rollback``/``complete``) plus the candidate and
112	predecessor existence, digest match and completeness when an intent is
113	valid, ``blocked``/``corrupt`` when the intent or a necessary artifact
114	is invalid, and ``failed``/``os-error`` when reading fails.
115	:func:`recover_many` is the controlled batch form of
116	:func:`recover_ledger` over the same kind of list: every path is
117	recovered in order, one ledger's failure never stops or rolls back the
118	others, a :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` becomes a ``blocked``/``corrupt``
119	item and an :class:`OSError` a ``failed``/``os-error`` item, and failed
120	ledgers keep their intent and artifacts so a re-run retries them
121	independently.  Both validate the whole list (a non-empty list of
122	non-empty, distinct strings) before any file is read or modified.
123	
124	:func:`apply_signed_remote` adds an offline-verifiable authentication
125	boundary in front of the same application flow.  It receives the ledger
126	path, a keyring, an envelope and the current moment.  The envelope
127	carries exactly ``node``, ``keyVersion``, ``request`` and ``signature``;
128	the request follows the :func:`apply_remote` contract and its ``source``
129	must equal the envelope's ``node``.  The keyring maps node names to
130	credential entries, each holding exactly ``version`` (a positive integer,
131	unique per node), ``secret`` (64 lowercase hex characters decoding to the
132	32-byte HMAC key), ``notBefore``/``notAfter`` (non-negative integers
133	bounding the validity period, both bounds inclusive) and ``revoked``.
134	The signed payload is the canonical compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of
135	``node``, ``keyVersion`` and ``request`` with every object key
136	recursively sorted lexicographically and non-ASCII preserved; the
137	signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 computed with the selected key
138	and compared in constant time.  Keys are selected by exact node and
139	version with no fallback: unknown credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid
140	or expired key, a source/node identity mismatch and a signature mismatch
141	all raise :class:`AuthenticationError` (a :class:`ValueError`) before the
142	ledger is ever read, so a failed verification creates no file.  Replays
143	are authenticated against the *current* keyring, so a later revocation or
144	expiry cannot be bypassed through a historical request binding.  Audit
145	entries committed through :func:`apply_signed_remote` record the verified
146	credentials under ``auth``; entries without ``auth`` remain readable and
147	:func:`apply_remote` keeps its public behaviour and ledger format.
148	
149	:func:`export_proof` and :func:`verify_proof` add offline audit-proof
150	exchange over the same ledger.  A proof is one version-1 UTF-8 compact
151	JSON object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
152	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level
153	keys ``digest``, ``endSeq``, ``entries``, ``firstBefore``, ``lastAfter``,
154	``startSeq`` and ``version``.  ``startSeq``/``endSeq`` name the covered
155	audit range, ``firstBefore`` is the state digest before the first covered
156	entry and ``lastAfter`` the state digest after the last one; ``entries``
157	hold the ledger entries in range unchanged, each carrying ``after``/
158	``before`` state digests, ``id``, ``seq`` and ``source`` with the optional
159	``auth`` binding.  ``digest`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact
160	canonical encoding (with no trailing newline) of the proof object with
161	the ``digest`` key itself removed.  :func:`verify_proof` is purely
162	offline: it reads neither the ledger nor the keyring.
163	
164	:func:`compare_proofs` relates two proofs offline, on top of that same
165	purely local verification.  Both arguments are :class:`bytes`; they are
166	first independently checked against the exact :func:`verify_proof`
167	contract, so a non-bytes argument raises :class:`TypeError` and either
168	proof being invalid raises :class:`InvalidProofError` before any
169	comparison.  The ledger, the keyring and the filesystem are never read
170	and neither input is modified.  The result is one version-1 UTF-8
171	compact JSON object -- every object key sorted lexicographically,
172	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the fixed
173	top-level keys ``common``, ``conflictSeq``, ``left``, ``overlap``,
174	``relation``, ``right`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
175	``left``/``right`` each carry the proof ``digest`` and its
176	``startSeq``/``endSeq``.  ``overlap`` is the closed shared seq interval
177	``[start, end]`` or ``null`` when the two ranges are disjoint; disjoint
178	ranges never raise and keep both sides' ranges.  With an overlap, the
179	complete entries at every shared seq are compared in ascending seq
180	order -- boundary and proof digests alone are never enough.  If every
181	shared entry matches, ``relation`` is ``"same"`` (identical ranges),
182	``"left-prefix"``/``"right-prefix"`` (same start and the shorter side
183	matches in full, named for the shorter side) or ``"overlap"``
184	otherwise; ``common`` then names the last shared boundary as
185	``{"after", "seq"}`` -- the last common entry's seq and after digest.
186	The first shared seq whose complete entry differs makes ``relation``
187	``"fork"`` with ``conflictSeq`` that earliest seq (never skipped past);
188	``common`` is the last equal entry when an equal entry precedes it, the
189	prior boundary ``{"after", "seq"}`` when the first shared entry already
190	conflicts but its ``before`` digests agree (its seq may be 0), and
191	``null`` when those ``before`` digests differ.  ``conflictSeq`` is
192	``null`` for every non-fork relation.  The bytes are deterministic for
193	equal inputs; swapping the inputs only exchanges ``left``/``right`` and
194	mirrors the prefix direction.
195	
196	:func:`plan_merge` turns that read-only comparison into a read-only merge
197	plan.  It takes both proof byte strings and a conflict ``policy`` --
198	``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"manual"``; any other value raises
199	:class:`ValueError` -- and validates every argument type before parsing
200	either proof, so a malformed proof never masks a :class:`TypeError` and an
201	invalid proof still raises :class:`InvalidProofError`.  Disjoint ranges,
202	or a fork whose common boundary cannot be confirmed, raise
203	:class:`ValueError` instead of producing a speculative plan.  Only
204	complete entries strictly after the common boundary become steps: an
205	unforked history accepts the longer side's tail as an ``extension``; a
206	fork accepts the selected side's tail (``selected``) and rejects the
207	other (``rejected``), while ``manual`` marks both tails ``manual`` and
208	references them from ``unresolved``.  The plan is one version-1 UTF-8
209	compact JSON object -- keys recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved,
210	exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level keys ``common``,
211	``left``, ``policy``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``, ``unresolved``
212	and ``version``; steps carry the original entries unchanged and are
213	ordered by ascending seq with the left side first on ties.  The plan is
214	byte-stable for equal inputs, mirrors left/right when the proofs are
215	swapped together with a ``left``/``right`` policy, and never touches the
216	filesystem or the inputs.
217	
218	:func:`resolve_merge` closes a ``manual`` plan read-only.  It takes the
219	plan byte string, the same two proofs and a list of decisions; only a
220	``manual`` plan produced by :func:`plan_merge` for exactly those proofs
221	may be resolved -- a plan from any other policy is a structurally valid
222	version-1 plan whose steps differ from the regenerated manual plan and
223	is therefore rejected as stale before any decision is considered.
224	A structurally invalid plan (encoding, duplicate keys, version-1
225	structure) raises :class:`InvalidPlanError`; a structurally valid plan
226	that is not byte-for-byte the manual plan regenerated from the proofs
227	(digest, relation, common boundary, side summaries, steps or unresolved
228	references) raises :class:`StalePlanError`; both are
229	:class:`ValueError` subclasses.  Each decision carries only ``side``,
230	``seq`` and ``action`` (``"accept"`` or ``"reject"``), resolving one
231	unresolved reference; missing, duplicate, extra or out-of-range
232	references and illegal choices raise :class:`InvalidResolutionError`
233	(a :class:`ValueError`).  Accepted entries must chain contiguously from
234	the common boundary -- at most one accepted side per seq, no acceptance
235	past a rejected seq, an unbroken seq and digest chain.  The result is
236	one version-1 compact JSON object with the top-level keys ``common``,
237	``left``, ``planDigest``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``,
238	``unresolved`` and ``version``; manual steps become
239	``accept``/``reject`` with the fixed reasons ``manual-accepted``/
240	``manual-rejected``, non-manual steps, carried audit entries and ``auth``
241	bindings are unchanged, ``unresolved`` is empty and ``planDigest`` is the
242	lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete source plan bytes.  Resolution is
243	deterministic, mirrors under a left/right swap with matching decisions,
244	and never touches the filesystem or the inputs.
245	
246	:func:`commit_resolution` is the write entry point that lands a manual
247	resolution in the ledger.  It takes the ledger path, the canonical
248	resolution bytes, the original plan bytes, both proofs and the landing
249	material -- the final ``state`` plus ``requests`` binding every accepted
250	entry id to its request digest.  Both proofs are verified offline and
251	the plan and resolution are checked against the freshly regenerated
252	manual plan (:class:`StalePlanError` otherwise, without touching the
253	ledger); the ledger itself must still sit at the resolution's common
254	boundary (:class:`StaleLedgerError`, a :class:`ValueError`).  A fully
255	identical replay is recognized before that staleness check and returns
256	``duplicate``; a resolution accepting nothing returns ``unchanged`` and
257	writes nothing.  Otherwise the final state, the request bindings and
258	the contiguous accepted entries -- rejected entries never enter the
259	audit -- are written in one fail-safe replacement, returning
260	``applied``.  The result carries only ``next``, ``resolutionDigest``
261	and ``status``.
262	"""

298	_MIN_LIMIT = 1
299	_MAX_LIMIT = 1000
300	_HEX64 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")
301	
302	
303	def export_batch(path: str, after: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> bytes:
304	    """Return one replication batch of audit records as UTF-8 JSON bytes.
305	
306	    Selects the first ``limit`` records whose ``seq`` is greater than
307	    ``after``.  ``after`` must not exceed the log's last seq (an empty or
308	    missing log has last seq 0); otherwise :class:`ValueError` is raised.
309	
310	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError` (``bool`` is not accepted as
311	    an int); ``after < 0`` or a ``limit`` outside ``[1, 1000]`` raises
312	    :class:`ValueError`.  A corrupt log raises
313	    :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.CorruptAuditError` and filesystem
314	    errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.  The log is never modified.
315	    """
316	    if not isinstance(path, str):
317	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
318	    if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int):
319	        raise TypeError("after must be an int")
320	    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
321	        raise TypeError("limit must be an int")
322	    if after < 0:
323	        raise ValueError("after must be >= 0")
324	    if limit < _MIN_LIMIT or limit > _MAX_LIMIT:
325	        raise ValueError("limit must be in [1, 1000]")
326	
327	    all_records = audit.read(path)
328	    last_seq = all_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if all_records else 0
329	    if after > last_seq:
330	        raise ValueError("after must not exceed the last audit seq")
331	
332	    selected = [record for record in all_records if record[audit.SEQ] > after]
333	    selected = selected[:limit]
334	    batch_records = [
335	        {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS} for record in selected
336	    ]
337	
338	    next_seq = batch_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if batch_records else after
339	    batch = {
340	        AFTER: after,
341	        COMPLETE: next_seq == last_seq,
342	        NEXT: next_seq,
343	        RECORDS: batch_records,
344	        VERSION: _BATCH_VERSION,
345	    }
346	    ordered = {key: batch[key] for key in _BATCH_KEYS}
347	    text = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
348	    return text.encode("utf-8")
349	
350	
351	def _invalid_batch(message: str) -> ValueError:
352	    return ValueError(f"invalid replication batch: {message}")
353	
354	
355	def _compact(obj: object) -> bytes:
356	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
357	
358	
359	def _parse_batch(batch: bytes) -> dict:
360	    """Validate a batch against the export byte contract and decode it."""
361	    if not batch.endswith(b"\n") or batch.endswith(b"\n\n"):
362	        raise _invalid_batch("must be a single JSON object terminated by one LF")
363	    try:
364	        data = json.loads(batch[:-1].decode("utf-8"))
365	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
366	        raise _invalid_batch("is not valid UTF-8 JSON") from exc
367	
368	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or tuple(data.keys()) != _BATCH_KEYS:
369	        raise _invalid_batch(
370	            "top-level object must have exactly the keys "
371	            "'after', 'complete', 'next', 'records', 'version' in order"
372	        )
373	    version = data[VERSION]
374	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != _BATCH_VERSION:
375	        raise _invalid_batch("version must be the integer 1")
376	    for key in (AFTER, NEXT):
377	        if isinstance(data[key], bool) or not isinstance(data[key], int):
378	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be an int")
379	        if data[key] < 0:
380	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be >= 0")
381	    if not isinstance(data[COMPLETE], bool):
382	        raise _invalid_batch("complete must be a bool")
383	    records = data[RECORDS]
384	    if not isinstance(records, list):
385	        raise _invalid_batch("records must be a list")
386	    if len(records) > _MAX_LIMIT:
387	        raise _invalid_batch("records must contain at most 1000 items")
388	    if not records and not data[COMPLETE]:
389	        raise _invalid_batch("empty records require complete to be true")
390	
391	    expected_seq = data[AFTER]
392	    expected_prev = audit._ZERO_HASH if data[AFTER] == 0 else None
393	    for index, record in enumerate(records):
394	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or tuple(record.keys()) != _RECORD_KEYS:
395	            raise _invalid_batch(
396	                f"record {index} must have exactly the keys "
397	                "'detail', 'hash', 'kind', 'prev', 'seq', 'source' in order"
398	            )
399	        # Only the byte contract is enforced here: key order, the
400	        # seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
401	        # (non-empty fields, the kind enum) belong to audit.append's event
402	        # input, so records from any log audit.read accepts stay importable.
403	        prev = record[audit.PREV]
404	        digest = record[audit.HASH]
405	        if expected_prev is not None:
406	            if prev != expected_prev:
407	                raise _invalid_batch(
408	                    f"record {index} prev does not match the previous record hash"
409	                )
410	        elif not isinstance(prev, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(prev):
411	            # The first record's prev refers to the exporter's log and
412	            # cannot be checked against local state; require hash shape.
413	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} prev must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
414	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
415	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
416	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} seq must be an int")
417	        expected_seq += 1
418	        if seq != expected_seq:
419	            raise _invalid_batch(
420	                f"record {index} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
421	            )
422	        without_hash = {
423	            audit.DETAIL: record[audit.DETAIL],
424	            audit.KIND: record[audit.KIND],
425	            audit.PREV: prev,
426	            audit.SEQ: seq,
427	            audit.SOURCE: record[audit.SOURCE],
428	        }
429	        if digest != audit._record_hash(without_hash):
430	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} hash does not match its contents")
431	        expected_prev = digest
432	
433	    expected_next = expected_seq if records else data[AFTER]
434	    if data[NEXT] != expected_next:
435	        raise _invalid_batch("next must be the last record seq, or after when empty")
436	
437	    # The bytes must be the exact canonical compact encoding export_batch
438	    # produces: no whitespace, no non-canonical escapes, fixed key order.
439	    if _compact(data) + b"\n" != batch:
440	        raise _invalid_batch("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
441	    return data

444	def _restore_log(path: str, existed: bool, size: int) -> None:
445	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed append.
446	
447	    Append-mode writes only ever extend the file, so truncating back to
448	    the pre-call size restores the exact prior bytes; a file the failed
449	    call newly created is unlinked again.  Rollback errors are swallowed
450	    so the original :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged.
451	    """
452	    try:
453	        if existed:
454	            with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
455	                handle.truncate(size)
456	                handle.flush()
457	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
458	        else:
459	            os.unlink(path)
460	    except OSError:
461	        pass
462	
463	
464	def import_batch(path: str, batch: bytes) -> dict:
465	    """Validate a replication batch and append its suffix to the local log.
466	
467	    See the module docstring for the byte contract.  A ``path`` that is not
468	    a str or a ``batch`` that is not bytes raises :class:`TypeError`; any
469	    contract violation raises :class:`ValueError`.  The local log is read
470	    solely through :func:`audit.read`, and a corrupt log or filesystem
471	    error propagates as :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
472	    CorruptAuditError` or :class:`OSError`.  Any failure leaves the log
473	    byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was
474	    missing).
475	    """
476	    if not isinstance(path, str):
477	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
478	    if not isinstance(batch, bytes):
479	        raise TypeError("batch must be bytes")
480	
481	    data = _parse_batch(batch)
482	    after = data[AFTER]
483	    batch_records = data[RECORDS]
484	
485	    local_records = audit.read(path)
486	    last_seq = local_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if local_records else 0
487	
488	    if after > last_seq:
489	        return {NEED: [last_seq + 1, after], NEXT: last_seq, STATUS: STATUS_MISSING}
490	
491	    # Records with seq <= last_seq must already exist locally and match the
492	    # batch record field by field; everything past last_seq is appended.
493	    suffix: list[dict] = []
494	    for record in batch_records:
495	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
496	        if seq <= last_seq:
497	            local = local_records[seq - 1]
498	            if any(record[key] != local[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS):
499	                raise _invalid_batch(
500	                    f"record {seq} conflicts with the local record of the same seq"
501	                )
502	        else:
503	            if seq != last_seq + 1 + len(suffix):
504	                raise _invalid_batch("records past the local last seq must be contiguous")
505	            suffix.append(record)
506	
507	    if not suffix:
508	        return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_DUPLICATE}
509	
510	    # The first appended record must chain onto the local log's last hash
511	    # (or the zero hash for an empty log).
512	    local_last_hash = local_records[-1][audit.HASH] if local_records else audit._ZERO_HASH
513	    if suffix[0][audit.PREV] != local_last_hash:
514	        raise _invalid_batch(
515	            "first new record prev must match the local last record hash"
516	        )
517	
518	    lines = b"".join(
519	        audit._encode_line({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS})
520	        for record in suffix
521	    )
522	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
523	    original_size = os.path.getsize(path) if existed else 0
524	    dir_fd: int | None = None
525	    try:
526	        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
527	            handle.write(lines)
528	            handle.flush()
529	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
530	        if not existed:
531	            dir_fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
532	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
533	    except OSError:
534	        _restore_log(path, existed, original_size)
535	        raise
536	    finally:
537	        if dir_fd is not None:
538	            os.close(dir_fd)
539	
540	    return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_APPLIED}

590	def _validated_apply_request(
591	    request: object,
592	) -> tuple[str, str, dict, dict]:
593	    """Validate an apply_remote request into (id, source, base, remote).
594	
595	    The states come back as fresh copies obeying the merge state contract,
596	    so type errors raised while validating them stay :class:`TypeError`.
597	    """
598	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
599	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
600	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
601	        raise ValueError(
602	            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'source', 'base' "
603	            "and 'remote'"
604	        )
605	    request_id = request[ID]
606	    source = request[SOURCE]
607	    if not isinstance(request_id, str):
608	        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
609	    if request_id == "":
610	        raise ValueError("request id must be non-empty")
611	    if not isinstance(source, str):
612	        raise TypeError("request source must be a str")
613	    if source == "":
614	        raise ValueError("request source must be non-empty")
615	    base_clock, base_records = merge._validated_state(request[BASE])
616	    remote_clock, remote_records = merge._validated_state(request[REMOTE])
617	    base = {merge.CLOCK: base_clock, merge.RECORDS: base_records}
618	    remote = {merge.CLOCK: remote_clock, merge.RECORDS: remote_records}
619	    return request_id, source, base, remote

622	def _request_digest(request_id: str, source: str, base: dict, remote: dict) -> str:
623	    """SHA-256 of the canonical compact encoding of the logical request."""
624	    ordered = {
625	        BASE: {merge.CLOCK: base[merge.CLOCK], merge.RECORDS: base[merge.RECORDS]},
626	        ID: request_id,
627	        REMOTE: {
628	            merge.CLOCK: remote[merge.CLOCK],
629	            merge.RECORDS: remote[merge.RECORDS],
630	        },
631	        SOURCE: source,
632	    }
633	    payload = json.dumps(
634	        ordered, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
635	    ).encode("utf-8")
636	    return _digest(payload)

642	    if AUTH in entry:
643	        out[AUTH] = {KEY_VERSION: entry[AUTH][KEY_VERSION], NODE: entry[AUTH][NODE]}

647	def _serialize_ledger(
648	    state: dict, requests: dict[str, str], entries: list[dict]
649	) -> bytes:
650	    """Canonical ledger bytes: compact JSON, sorted keys, one trailing LF."""
651	    ledger = {
652	        AUDIT: [_serialize_entry(entry) for entry in entries],
653	        REQUESTS: dict(requests),
654	        STATE_KEY: {
655	            merge.CLOCK: state[merge.CLOCK],
656	            merge.RECORDS: state[merge.RECORDS],
657	        },
658	        "version": LEDGER_VERSION,
659	    }
660	    text = json.dumps(
661	        ledger, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
662	    ) + "\n"
663	    return text.encode("utf-8")

666	def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
667	    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None

670	def _parse_ledger(raw: bytes) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, str], list[dict]]:
671	    """Validate every byte of a ledger into (state, requests, audit).
672	
673	    Any decoding, structural, state, index or chain violation raises
674	    :class:`ValueError`; in particular a type fault in the stored state is
675	    an on-disk corruption, not a :class:`TypeError`.
676	    """
677	    try:
678	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
679	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
680	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
681	    try:
682	        data = json.loads(text)
683	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
684	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc
685	
686	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
687	        raise _ledger_invalid("must be a JSON object")
688	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_LEDGER_TOP_KEYS):
689	        raise _ledger_invalid(
690	            "must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'requests', 'state' "
691	            "and 'version'"
692	        )
693	    version = data["version"]
694	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
695	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be an int")
696	    if version != LEDGER_VERSION:
697	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be the integer 1")
698	
699	    try:
700	        clock, records = merge._validated_state(data[STATE_KEY])
701	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
702	        raise _ledger_invalid(f"state is invalid: {exc}") from exc
703	    state = {merge.CLOCK: clock, merge.RECORDS: records}
704	
705	    raw_requests = data[REQUESTS]
706	    if not isinstance(raw_requests, dict):
707	        raise _ledger_invalid("requests must be a JSON object")
708	    requests: dict[str, str] = {}
709	    for bound_id, bound_digest in raw_requests.items():
710	        if not isinstance(bound_id, str) or bound_id == "":
711	            raise _ledger_invalid("requests keys must be non-empty str")
712	        if not _is_digest(bound_digest):
713	            raise _ledger_invalid(
714	                "requests values must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
715	            )
716	        requests[bound_id] = bound_digest
717	
718	    raw_entries = data[AUDIT]
719	    if not isinstance(raw_entries, list):
720	        raise _ledger_invalid("audit must be an array")
721	    entries: list[dict] = []
722	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
723	    expected_seq = 1
724	    expected_before: str | None = None
725	    for position, entry in enumerate(raw_entries):
726	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
727	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} must be an object")
728	        entry_keys = set(entry.keys())
729	        if entry_keys != _LEDGER_ENTRY_KEY_SET and entry_keys != _LEDGER_ENTRY_AUTHED_SET:
730	            raise _ledger_invalid(
731	                f"audit entry {position} must contain exactly the keys "
732	                "'after', 'before', 'id', 'seq' and 'source' with "
733	                "optional 'auth'"
734	            )
735	        after_digest = entry[AFTER]
736	        before_digest = entry[BEFORE]
737	        entry_id = entry[ID]
738	        seq = entry["seq"]
739	        entry_source = entry[SOURCE]
740	        if not _is_digest(after_digest):
741	            raise _ledger_invalid(
742	                f"audit entry {position} after must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
743	            )
744	        if not _is_digest(before_digest):
745	            raise _ledger_invalid(
746	                f"audit entry {position} before must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
747	            )
748	        if not isinstance(entry_id, str) or entry_id == "":
749	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} id must be a non-empty str")
750	        if not isinstance(entry_source, str) or entry_source == "":
751	            raise _ledger_invalid(
752	                f"audit entry {position} source must be a non-empty str"
753	            )
754	        parsed_auth = None
755	        if AUTH in entry:
756	            # Entries committed through apply_signed_remote carry the
757	            # credentials they were verified against; entries written by
758	            # plain apply_remote have none and stay readable.
759	            auth = entry[AUTH]
760	            if not isinstance(auth, dict) or set(auth.keys()) != _LEDGER_AUTH_KEYS:
761	                raise _ledger_invalid(
762	                    f"audit entry {position} auth must contain exactly the "
763	                    "keys 'keyVersion' and 'node'"
764	                )
765	            auth_node = auth[NODE]
766	            auth_version = auth[KEY_VERSION]
767	            if not isinstance(auth_node, str) or auth_node == "":
768	                raise _ledger_invalid(
769	                    f"audit entry {position} auth node must be a non-empty str"
770	                )
771	            if (
772	                isinstance(auth_version, bool)
773	                or not isinstance(auth_version, int)
774	                or auth_version <= 0
775	            ):
776	                raise _ledger_invalid(
777	                    f"audit entry {position} auth keyVersion must be a "
778	                    "positive int"
779	                )
780	            parsed_auth = {KEY_VERSION: auth_version, NODE: auth_node}
781	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
782	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} seq must be an int")
783	        if seq != expected_seq:
784	            raise _ledger_invalid(
785	                f"audit entry {position} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
786	            )
787	        if entry_id in seen_ids:
788	            raise _ledger_invalid(
789	                f"audit entry {position} repeats the already applied id {entry_id!r}"
790	            )
791	        if entry_id not in requests:
792	            raise _ledger_invalid(
793	                f"audit entry {position} id {entry_id!r} is missing from requests"
794	            )
795	        if expected_before is not None and before_digest != expected_before:
796	            raise _ledger_invalid(
797	                f"audit entry {position} before does not chain to the previous after"
798	            )
799	        parsed_entry = {
800	            AFTER: after_digest,
801	            BEFORE: before_digest,
802	            ID: entry_id,
803	            "seq": seq,
804	            SOURCE: entry_source,
805	        }
806	        if parsed_auth is not None:
807	            parsed_entry[AUTH] = parsed_auth
808	        entries.append(parsed_entry)
809	        seen_ids.add(entry_id)
810	        expected_seq += 1
811	        expected_before = after_digest
812	
813	    if seen_ids != set(requests):
814	        raise _ledger_invalid("requests and audit must bind the same ids")
815	    if entries and entries[-1][AFTER] != _digest(_state_bytes(state)):
816	        raise _ledger_invalid("last audit after must hash the stored state")
817	
818	    # The bytes must be the single canonical compact encoding with sorted
819	    # keys and exactly one trailing newline.
820	    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
821	        raise _ledger_invalid("must end with exactly one newline")
822	    if _serialize_ledger(state, requests, entries) != raw:
823	        raise _ledger_invalid("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
824	    return state, requests, entries

827	def _read_ledger(
828	    path: str, base: dict
829	) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, str], list[dict]]:
830	    """Load the ledger at ``path``; a missing file stands for ``base``."""
831	    try:
832	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
833	            raw = handle.read()
834	    except FileNotFoundError:
835	        clock, records = merge._validated_state(base)
836	        return {merge.CLOCK: clock, merge.RECORDS: records}, {}, []
837	    return _parse_ledger(raw)

840	def _record_decision(
841	    local_clock: dict,
842	    local_record: list | None,
843	    remote_record: list,
844	) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
845	    """Classify one remote record against the current local state."""
846	    need = merge._remote_need(remote_record, local_clock)
847	    if need:
848	        return STATUS_MISSING, need
849	    if local_record is None:
850	        return APPLY, None
851	    if local_record == remote_record:
852	        return STATUS_DUPLICATE, None
853	    if merge._dominates(remote_record[2], local_record[2]):
854	        return APPLY, None

897	def _rollback_ledger_write(
898	    path: str,
899	    tmp_path: str | None,
900	    backup_path: str | None,
901	    existed: bool,
902	    stage: str,
903	    original: bytes | None,
904	) -> None:
905	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed :func:`_atomic_write`.
906	
907	    ``stage`` records how far the transaction got: ``write`` (temporary
908	    file written), ``link`` (predecessor hard-linked aside), ``intent``
909	    (the prepared recovery intent published), ``install`` (temporary
910	    moved into place), ``sync`` (the directory sync after install),
911	    ``confirm`` (the installed intent published), ``cleanup`` (the
912	    predecessor link removed) or ``final`` (the intent removed, its
913	    directory sync failed).  The predecessor is retained as a hard link
914	    rather than rewritten, so renaming it back restores the original
915	    file byte-for-byte (indeed as the same inode) even with no working
916	    fsync or free space left; once that link is already gone, the
917	    captured pre-call bytes are rewritten from memory instead.  The
918	    recovery intent at ``path + ".txn"`` only ever belongs to the failed
919	    call and is removed as well.  The directory is synced last so the
920	    recovery is durable.  Every recovery error is swallowed so the
921	    original exception propagates unchanged.
922	    """
923	    try:
924	        if stage in ("cleanup", "final"):
925	            # The new ledger was installed and the install synced; only
926	            # the backup removal, the intent removal or a directory sync
927	            # failed.  The commit still must not stand: rename the
928	            # retained link back when it survives, otherwise rewrite the
929	            # captured pre-call bytes from memory.
930	            _remove_quietly(tmp_path)
931	            if backup_path is not None and os.path.exists(backup_path):
932	                os.replace(backup_path, path)
933	            elif original is not None:
934	                _restore_bytes_quietly(path, original)
935	            else:
936	                try:
937	                    os.unlink(path)
938	                except FileNotFoundError:
939	                    pass
940	        elif stage in ("sync", "confirm"):
941	            _remove_quietly(tmp_path)
942	            if existed:
943	                os.replace(backup_path, path)
944	            else:
945	                try:
946	                    os.unlink(path)
947	                except FileNotFoundError:
948	                    pass
949	        elif stage in ("install", "intent"):
950	            # The replacement did not run: the predecessor at path is
951	            # untouched; the backup link and temporary file are internal
952	            # artifacts to remove.
953	            if backup_path is not None:
954	                try:
955	                    os.unlink(backup_path)
956	                except FileNotFoundError:
957	                    pass
958	            if tmp_path is not None:
959	                try:
960	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
961	                except FileNotFoundError:
962	                    pass
963	        else:
964	            # write/link stages leave the predecessor in place; the link
965	            # stage additionally leaves a backup link to remove.
966	            if tmp_path is not None:
967	                try:
968	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
969	                except FileNotFoundError:
970	                    pass
971	            if stage == "link" and backup_path is not None:
972	                try:
973	                    os.unlink(backup_path)
974	                except FileNotFoundError:
975	                    pass
976	        # The recovery intent only ever belongs to this transaction.
977	        _remove_quietly(path + ".txn")
978	        try:
979	            storage._fsync_dir(path)
980	        except OSError:
981	            pass
982	    except OSError:
983	        pass

994	def _reserve_unique_file(prefix: str) -> tuple[BinaryIO, str]:
995	    """Open a fresh file named ``prefix + <random hex>``, exclusively."""
996	    last_error: OSError | None = None

1009	    """Open a fresh, uniquely named transaction file next to ``path``.
1010	
1011	    Exclusive binary create (``"xb"``) atomically reserves a random name
1012	    and gives the file the same mode a plain create would; a collision

1019	def _link_predecessor_aside(path: str) -> str:
1020	    """Hard-link the existing ledger to a unique backup name.
1021	
1022	    ``os.link`` is atomic and fails with :class:`FileExistsError` when the
1023	    candidate name already exists (for example as a leftover of a killed
1024	    transaction), so the name can be reserved by the link itself without
1025	    any create-then-link window.
1026	    """
1027	    last_error: OSError | None = None
1028	    for _ in range(128):

1030	        try:
1031	            os.link(path, backup_path)
1032	        except FileExistsError as exc:
1033	            last_error = exc
1034	            continue
1035	        return backup_path
1036	    # Practically unreachable: 128 random 64-bit name collisions in a row.
1037	    raise last_error if last_error is not None else OSError(
1038	        "could not reserve a ledger backup file name"
1039	    )

1143	def _parse_intent(raw: bytes, ledger_base: str) -> dict:
1144	    """Validate every byte of a recovery intent and return its decoded form.
1145	
1146	    Any decoding, structural, phase, name or digest violation raises
1147	    :class:`CorruptRecoveryError`.
1148	    """
1149	    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
1150	        raise _recovery_invalid("must be a single JSON object ending in one LF")
1151	    try:
1152	        text = raw[:-1].decode("utf-8")
1153	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
1154	        raise _recovery_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
1155	    try:
1156	        data = json.loads(text)
1157	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
1158	        raise _recovery_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc
1159	
1160	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != _INTENT_KEYS:
1161	        raise _recovery_invalid(
1162	            "must contain exactly the keys 'candidate', 'newDigest', "
1163	            "'oldDigest', 'phase', 'predecessor' and 'version'"
1164	        )
1165	    version = data[VERSION]
1166	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
1167	        raise _recovery_invalid("version must be an int")
1168	    if version != RECOVERY_VERSION:
1169	        raise _recovery_invalid("version must be the integer 1")
1170	    phase = data[INTENT_PHASE]
1171	    if phase not in (PHASE_PREPARED, PHASE_INSTALLED):
1172	        raise _recovery_invalid("phase must be 'prepared' or 'installed'")
1173	    if not _is_digest(data[INTENT_NEW_DIGEST]):
1174	        raise _recovery_invalid("newDigest must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
1175	    old_digest = data[INTENT_OLD_DIGEST]
1176	    if old_digest is not None and not _is_digest(old_digest):
1177	        raise _recovery_invalid(
1178	            "oldDigest must be null or 64 lowercase hex characters"
1179	        )
1180	    _validated_artifact_name(data[INTENT_CANDIDATE], "candidate", ledger_base)
1181	    predecessor = data[INTENT_PREDECESSOR]
1182	    if predecessor is not None:
1183	        _validated_artifact_name(predecessor, "predecessor", ledger_base)
1184	    if (old_digest is None) != (predecessor is None):
1185	        raise _recovery_invalid(
1186	            "oldDigest and predecessor must both be null or both be set"
1187	        )
1188	
1189	    # The bytes must be the single canonical compact encoding with
1190	    # recursively sorted keys and exactly one trailing newline.
1191	    if _intent_compact(data) + b"\n" != raw:
1192	        raise _recovery_invalid("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
1193	    return data

1196	def recover_ledger(path: str) -> dict:
1197	    """Reconcile an interrupted ledger transaction at ``path``.
1198	
1199	    When no recovery intent exists at ``path + ".txn"`` the result is
1200	    ``clean`` and no random artifacts are scanned.  Otherwise the intent
1201	    is fully validated -- a parse, field, phase, name, digest or
1202	    necessary-artifact violation raises :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` (a
1203	    :class:`ValueError`) without touching the ledger or any unrelated
1204	    file -- and the interrupted transaction is settled by its phase:
1205	
1206	    - ``prepared``: the commit was never confirmed.  The old bytes are
1207	      kept or restored byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the
1208	      path stays missing when it was missing) and the referenced new
1209	      candidate is deleted; the status is ``rolled-back``.
1210	    - ``installed``: the new ledger already replaced the old one and the
1211	      directory synced.  The current bytes must hash to ``newDigest``;
1212	      the remaining referenced artifacts are cleaned and the status is
1213	      ``completed``.
1214	
1215	    Only files the intent references are removed, the intent itself is
1216	    deleted last and the directory is synced, so a repeated call reports
1217	    ``clean``.  The result is a fresh dict with the key order ``digest``,
1218	    ``status``; ``digest`` is the digest of the resulting ledger bytes,
1219	    or ``None`` when the path is missing.  A ``path`` that is not a str
1220	    raises :class:`TypeError`; an :class:`OSError` while reading,
1221	    replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with enough
1222	    intent and artifacts left in place for a retry.
1223	    """
1224	    if not isinstance(path, str):
1225	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
1226	    try:
1227	        with open(path + ".txn", "rb") as handle:
1228	            raw = handle.read()
1229	    except FileNotFoundError:
1230	        # No intent: nothing to settle, and random leftover artifacts
1231	        # are never scanned.  The digest still summarizes the ledger
1232	        # bytes currently at the path (None when the path is missing).
1233	        try:
1234	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1235	                current = handle.read()
1236	        except FileNotFoundError:
1237	            current = None
1238	        return {
1239	            "digest": _digest(current) if current is not None else None,
1240	            STATUS: STATUS_CLEAN,
1241	        }
1242	
1243	    ledger_base = os.path.basename(path)
1244	    intent = _parse_intent(raw, ledger_base)
1245	    phase = intent[INTENT_PHASE]
1246	    new_digest = intent[INTENT_NEW_DIGEST]
1247	    old_digest = intent[INTENT_OLD_DIGEST]
1248	    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
1249	    candidate_path = os.path.join(directory, intent[INTENT_CANDIDATE])
1250	    predecessor_path = (
1251	        os.path.join(directory, intent[INTENT_PREDECESSOR])
1252	        if intent[INTENT_PREDECESSOR] is not None
1253	        else None
1254	    )
1255	
1256	    try:
1257	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1258	            current = handle.read()
1259	    except FileNotFoundError:
1260	        current = None
1261	
1262	    # Every validation finishes before the first mutation, so a
1263	    # CorruptRecoveryError never changes the ledger or any other file.
1264	    restore = False
1265	    remove_path = False
1266	    if phase == PHASE_PREPARED:
1267	        current_digest = _digest(current) if current is not None else None
1268	        if old_digest is None:
1269	            # The path was missing: it may only hold the unconfirmed new
1270	            # bytes (the replacement already ran) and must be missing
1271	            # again after the rollback.
1272	            if current is not None:
1273	                if current_digest != new_digest:
1274	                    raise _recovery_invalid(
1275	                        "ledger bytes do not match newDigest"
1276	                    )
1277	                remove_path = True
1278	        elif current_digest != old_digest:
1279	            if current_digest is not None and current_digest != new_digest:
1280	                raise _recovery_invalid(
1281	                    "ledger bytes match neither oldDigest nor newDigest"
1282	                )
1283	            # The old bytes must come back byte-for-byte from the
1284	            # retained predecessor (also when the path vanished).
1285	            try:
1286	                with open(predecessor_path, "rb") as handle:
1287	                    predecessor = handle.read()
1288	            except FileNotFoundError as exc:
1289	                raise _recovery_invalid(
1290	                    "predecessor artifact is missing"
1291	                ) from exc
1292	            if _digest(predecessor) != old_digest:
1293	                raise _recovery_invalid(
1294	                    "predecessor artifact does not match oldDigest"
1295	                )
1296	            restore = True
1297	    else:
1298	        # installed: the new ledger is the durable content and must
1299	        # still hash to the confirmed digest.
1300	        if current is None:
1301	            raise _recovery_invalid("ledger is missing the installed bytes")
1302	        if _digest(current) != new_digest:
1303	            raise _recovery_invalid(
1304	                "ledger bytes do not match the installed newDigest"
1305	            )
1306	
1307	    # Settle the transaction.  The intent survives every failure here
1308	    # (it is deleted last), so an OSError leaves enough state to retry.
1309	    if restore:
1310	        os.replace(predecessor_path, path)
1311	        predecessor_path = None
1312	    elif remove_path:
1313	        os.unlink(path)
1314	    for artifact in (candidate_path, predecessor_path):
1315	        if artifact is None:
1316	            continue
1317	        try:
1318	            os.unlink(artifact)
1319	        except FileNotFoundError:
1320	            pass
1321	    storage._fsync_dir(path)
1322	    os.unlink(path + ".txn")
1323	    storage._fsync_dir(path)
1324	
1325	    if phase == PHASE_PREPARED:
1326	        return {"digest": old_digest, STATUS: STATUS_ROLLED_BACK}
1327	    return {"digest": new_digest, STATUS: STATUS_COMPLETED}

"""Read-only audit replication batches.

A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::

    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}

The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.

:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.

Batches are checked only against the byte contract: canonical encoding, key
order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the kind enum, non-empty
string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every log :func:`audit.read`
accepts round-trips through :func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The
append itself is atomic: when the write, flush or fsync step raises
:class:`OSError` the error propagates unchanged and the log is left
byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was missing).

:func:`apply_remote` persists remote state applications in a version-1
*ledger*: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys sorted lexicographically,
exactly one trailing ``\\n``) with the top-level keys ``audit``,
``requests``, ``state`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
``state`` holds the current :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state,
``requests`` binds each accepted request id to the digest of its request,
and ``audit`` lists one entry per successful application in order; each
entry carries ``after``/``before`` state digests, the request ``id`` and
``source`` and a contiguous ``seq`` starting at 1, every entry after the
first chaining its ``before`` to the previous entry's ``after`` and the
last ``after`` hashing the stored state.  A missing ledger stands for the
request's ``base`` state with empty indexes; any existing file that fails
the byte, structure, state or index rules is rejected with
:class:`ValueError` and left untouched.

Replaying a request whose ``id`` is already bound to exactly the same
request digest always yields ``duplicate`` from the saved binding alone,
immediately or after other commits: one item per remote record in
ascending key order, each already duplicate with an empty ``need`` map,
and no receipt; the ledger is never read for modification on a replay.
A bound ``id`` presented with a different request raises
:class:`ValueError`.  Every successful commit is one durable transaction:
write, flush, file sync, replacement and directory sync all lie inside
its boundary, and an :class:`OSError` at any stage propagates unchanged
with the file system restored to its pre-call state.

Each commit is additionally backed by a *recovery intent* so a crash of
the committing process itself can be reconciled later, across processes.
Before anything is replaced, the commit publishes an intent at ``path +
".txn"``: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys recursively sorted,
exactly one trailing ``\n``) recording only ``version`` (the integer 1),
``phase``, the lowercase hex SHA-256 digests of the new and old ledger
bytes (``newDigest``/``oldDigest``) and the safe base names of the
candidate and predecessor transaction files, all confined to the
ledger's own directory; when the ledger did not exist, ``oldDigest`` and
``predecessor`` are both ``null``.  The intent starts in phase
``prepared`` and is republished as ``installed`` only after the new
ledger has replaced the old one and the directory has synced; the
intent's own creation and phase change each sync the file and the
directory.  A crash before the ``installed`` intent is durable leaves
the commit unconfirmed: :func:`recover_ledger` keeps or restores the old
bytes (byte-for-byte, and missing again when the path was missing) and
deletes the referenced candidate.  A crash afterwards lets
:func:`recover_ledger` verify the new bytes against ``newDigest`` and
finish the cleanup.  Only files the intent references are removed, the
intent itself is deleted last and the directory is synced, and a
repeated call reports ``clean`` without scanning random artifacts.

:func:`recover_ledger` returns a fresh dict with the key order
``digest``, ``status``: ``clean`` when no intent exists, ``rolled-back``
or ``completed`` after a recovery, with ``digest`` holding the digest of
the resulting ledger bytes (``None`` when the path is missing).  A
``path`` that is not a str raises :class:`TypeError`; an intent that
fails to parse, or whose fields, phase, names, digests or necessary
artifacts are invalid, raises :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` (a
:class:`ValueError`) without touching the ledger or any unrelated file;
an :class:`OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing
propagates unchanged with enough intent and artifacts left for a retry.
The ledger write entry points run this recovery automatically after
their input validation, before the ledger is read.

:func:`inspect_recovery` diagnoses an explicit, non-empty list of ledger
paths without modifying anything: only each listed ledger, its intent
and the artifacts the intent references are read.  Each report carries
``path``, ``status``, ``phase``, ``digest``, ``artifacts``, ``action``
and ``error`` -- ``clean`` with a null phase and action when no intent
exists (the digest still summarizes the ledger bytes, or is null when
the path is missing), ``pending`` with the intent's phase and the
suggested action (``rollback``/``complete``) plus the candidate and
predecessor existence, digest match and completeness when an intent is
valid, ``blocked``/``corrupt`` when the intent or a necessary artifact
is invalid, and ``failed``/``os-error`` when reading fails.
:func:`recover_many` is the controlled batch form of
:func:`recover_ledger` over the same kind of list: every path is
recovered in order, one ledger's failure never stops or rolls back the
others, a :class:`CorruptRecoveryError` becomes a ``blocked``/``corrupt``
item and an :class:`OSError` a ``failed``/``os-error`` item, and failed
ledgers keep their intent and artifacts so a re-run retries them
independently.  Both validate the whole list (a non-empty list of
non-empty, distinct strings) before any file is read or modified.

:func:`apply_signed_remote` adds an offline-verifiable authentication
boundary in front of the same application flow.  It receives the ledger
path, a keyring, an envelope and the current moment.  The envelope
carries exactly ``node``, ``keyVersion``, ``request`` and ``signature``;
the request follows the :func:`apply_remote` contract and its ``source``
must equal the envelope's ``node``.  The keyring maps node names to
credential entries, each holding exactly ``version`` (a positive integer,
unique per node), ``secret`` (64 lowercase hex characters decoding to the
32-byte HMAC key), ``notBefore``/``notAfter`` (non-negative integers
bounding the validity period, both bounds inclusive) and ``revoked``.
The signed payload is the canonical compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of
``node``, ``keyVersion`` and ``request`` with every object key
recursively sorted lexicographically and non-ASCII preserved; the
signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 computed with the selected key
and compared in constant time.  Keys are selected by exact node and
version with no fallback: unknown credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid
or expired key, a source/node identity mismatch and a signature mismatch
all raise :class:`AuthenticationError` (a :class:`ValueError`) before the
ledger is ever read, so a failed verification creates no file.  Replays
are authenticated against the *current* keyring, so a later revocation or
expiry cannot be bypassed through a historical request binding.  Audit
entries committed through :func:`apply_signed_remote` record the verified
credentials under ``auth``; entries without ``auth`` remain readable and
:func:`apply_remote` keeps its public behaviour and ledger format.

:func:`export_proof` and :func:`verify_proof` add offline audit-proof
exchange over the same ledger.  A proof is one version-1 UTF-8 compact
JSON object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level
keys ``digest``, ``endSeq``, ``entries``, ``firstBefore``, ``lastAfter``,
``startSeq`` and ``version``.  ``startSeq``/``endSeq`` name the covered
audit range, ``firstBefore`` is the state digest before the first covered
entry and ``lastAfter`` the state digest after the last one; ``entries``
hold the ledger entries in range unchanged, each carrying ``after``/
``before`` state digests, ``id``, ``seq`` and ``source`` with the optional
``auth`` binding.  ``digest`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact
canonical encoding (with no trailing newline) of the proof object with
the ``digest`` key itself removed.  :func:`verify_proof` is purely
offline: it reads neither the ledger nor the keyring.

:func:`compare_proofs` relates two proofs offline, on top of that same
purely local verification.  Both arguments are :class:`bytes`; they are
first independently checked against the exact :func:`verify_proof`
contract, so a non-bytes argument raises :class:`TypeError` and either
proof being invalid raises :class:`InvalidProofError` before any
comparison.  The ledger, the keyring and the filesystem are never read
and neither input is modified.  The result is one version-1 UTF-8
compact JSON object -- every object key sorted lexicographically,
non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the fixed
top-level keys ``common``, ``conflictSeq``, ``left``, ``overlap``,
``relation``, ``right`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
``left``/``right`` each carry the proof ``digest`` and its
``startSeq``/``endSeq``.  ``overlap`` is the closed shared seq interval
``[start, end]`` or ``null`` when the two ranges are disjoint; disjoint
ranges never raise and keep both sides' ranges.  With an overlap, the
complete entries at every shared seq are compared in ascending seq
order -- boundary and proof digests alone are never enough.  If every
shared entry matches, ``relation`` is ``"same"`` (identical ranges),
``"left-prefix"``/``"right-prefix"`` (same start and the shorter side
matches in full, named for the shorter side) or ``"overlap"``
otherwise; ``common`` then names the last shared boundary as
``{"after", "seq"}`` -- the last common entry's seq and after digest.
The first shared seq whose complete entry differs makes ``relation``
``"fork"`` with ``conflictSeq`` that earliest seq (never skipped past);
``common`` is the last equal entry when an equal entry precedes it, the
prior boundary ``{"after", "seq"}`` when the first shared entry already
conflicts but its ``before`` digests agree (its seq may be 0), and
``null`` when those ``before`` digests differ.  ``conflictSeq`` is
``null`` for every non-fork relation.  The bytes are deterministic for
equal inputs; swapping the inputs only exchanges ``left``/``right`` and
mirrors the prefix direction.

:func:`plan_merge` turns that read-only comparison into a read-only merge
plan.  It takes both proof byte strings and a conflict ``policy`` --
``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"manual"``; any other value raises
:class:`ValueError` -- and validates every argument type before parsing
either proof, so a malformed proof never masks a :class:`TypeError` and an
invalid proof still raises :class:`InvalidProofError`.  Disjoint ranges,
or a fork whose common boundary cannot be confirmed, raise
:class:`ValueError` instead of producing a speculative plan.  Only
complete entries strictly after the common boundary become steps: an
unforked history accepts the longer side's tail as an ``extension``; a
fork accepts the selected side's tail (``selected``) and rejects the
other (``rejected``), while ``manual`` marks both tails ``manual`` and
references them from ``unresolved``.  The plan is one version-1 UTF-8
compact JSON object -- keys recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved,
exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level keys ``common``,
``left``, ``policy``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``, ``unresolved``
and ``version``; steps carry the original entries unchanged and are
ordered by ascending seq with the left side first on ties.  The plan is
byte-stable for equal inputs, mirrors left/right when the proofs are
swapped together with a ``left``/``right`` policy, and never touches the
filesystem or the inputs.

:func:`resolve_merge` closes a ``manual`` plan read-only.  It takes the
plan byte string, the same two proofs and a list of decisions; only a
``manual`` plan produced by :func:`plan_merge` for exactly those proofs
may be resolved -- a plan from any other policy is a structurally valid
version-1 plan whose steps differ from the regenerated manual plan and
is therefore rejected as stale before any decision is considered.
A structurally invalid plan (encoding, duplicate keys, version-1
structure) raises :class:`InvalidPlanError`; a structurally valid plan
that is not byte-for-byte the manual plan regenerated from the proofs
(digest, relation, common boundary, side summaries, steps or unresolved
references) raises :class:`StalePlanError`; both are
:class:`ValueError` subclasses.  Each decision carries only ``side``,
``seq`` and ``action`` (``"accept"`` or ``"reject"``), resolving one
unresolved reference; missing, duplicate, extra or out-of-range
references and illegal choices raise :class:`InvalidResolutionError`
(a :class:`ValueError`).  Accepted entries must chain contiguously from
the common boundary -- at most one accepted side per seq, no acceptance
past a rejected seq, an unbroken seq and digest chain.  The result is
one version-1 compact JSON object with the top-level keys ``common``,
``left``, ``planDigest``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``,
``unresolved`` and ``version``; manual steps become
``accept``/``reject`` with the fixed reasons ``manual-accepted``/
``manual-rejected``, non-manual steps, carried audit entries and ``auth``
bindings are unchanged, ``unresolved`` is empty and ``planDigest`` is the
lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete source plan bytes.  Resolution is
deterministic, mirrors under a left/right swap with matching decisions,
and never touches the filesystem or the inputs.

:func:`commit_resolution` is the write entry point that lands a manual
resolution in the ledger.  It takes the ledger path, the canonical
resolution bytes, the original plan bytes, both proofs and the landing
material -- the final ``state`` plus ``requests`` binding every accepted
entry id to its request digest.  Both proofs are verified offline and
the plan and resolution are checked against the freshly regenerated
manual plan (:class:`StalePlanError` otherwise, without touching the
ledger); the ledger itself must still sit at the resolution's common
boundary (:class:`StaleLedgerError`, a :class:`ValueError`).  A fully
identical replay is recognized before that staleness check and returns
``duplicate``; a resolution accepting nothing returns ``unchanged`` and
writes nothing.  Otherwise the final state, the request bindings and
the contiguous accepted entries -- rejected entries never enter the
audit -- are written in one fail-safe replacement, returning
``applied``.  The result carries only ``next``, ``resolutionDigest``
and ``status``.
